title: Normalization Equivariance for Arbitrary Backbones, with Application to Image Denoising
claim: Wrapping any backbone with parameter-free normalize and denormalize steps yields exact equivariance without changing the backbone's internals.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right chain, skip arrow carrying statistics beneath
description: A single wide rounded gray container holds a left-to-right chain. Input y enters from the left, and a dot on the arrow splits off a branch. The main path runs through an orange box T_NE, then a labeled intermediate ỹ, then a large blue-outlined lavender box g_θ (the arbitrary backbone). It then passes through a second orange box T_NE^{-1} and exits as x̂ on the right. The branch runs below as a curved gray arrow labeled μ(y), std(y). It feeds the statistics into the inverse transform box. Orange marks the parameter-free wrapper steps and blue marks the backbone, so the eye lands on the central blue box. The figure is sparse, with large math notation.
caption: Normalization-equivariant wrapper (WNE). Given a noisy input y, we compute instance statistics µ(y) and std(y), normalize to ˜y = TNE(y), apply an arbitrary backbone gθ, and denormalize with the stored statistics to produce ˆx = std(y) gθ(˜y) + µ(y)1. This enforces input-output normalization equivariance without modifying the backbone.
abstract: Normalization Equivariance (NE) is a structural prior that improves robustness to distribution shift in image-to-image tasks. A function $f$ is normalization equivariant iff $f(a y + b\mathbf{1}) = a f(y) + b\mathbf{1}$ for all $a>0$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}$. Existing NE methods constrain every internal layer to NE-compatible operations. These constraints add runtime cost and exclude standard transformer components such as softmax attention and LayerNorm. We introduce Wrapped Normalization Equivariance (WNE), a parameter-free wrapper that normalizes the input, applies any backbone, and denormalizes the output. We prove every NE function admits this factorization, so the wrapper exactly parameterizes the class of NE functions. On blind denoising, wrapping CNN and transformer architectures improves robustness under noise-level mismatch with no measurable GPU overhead, while architectural NE baselines are up to $1.6\times$ slower.
